prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Signing in ensures your pet status and collection are safely saved to your cloud account."]
1: ["Quick Desktop Pet Controls", "Learn how to summon, feed, or hide your new pet directly from your desktop system tray.", "Right-click system tray to hide/show pet", "Click pet directly to open interaction menu"]
2: ["Ensure single subject, good lighting, and clear front view for optimal pet generation result."]
3: ["Your Pet is Ready on Your Desktop!", "If you don't see your pet wandering around, check your taskbar or click locate pet.", "Locate Pet on Desktop"]
4: ["Preparing Your New Companion", "We are generating your pet graphics. We will send a desktop notification when ready."]
5: ["Choose Your Companion's Journey", "Scroll through available companion paths and select your preferred adventure."]
6: []
7: ["Quick Instant Sign-In"]
8: ["Did you know? You can customize pet sounds in settings later."]
9: ["Welcome to Your Virtual Desktop Companion", "Get ready to adopt a pet that lives directly on your desktop."]
